executive_summary: This is a 2005-era Visual Basic 6.0 desktop CRM application backed by a Microsoft Access database on an SMB file share. It has no modern software engineering practices — no CI/CD, no tests, no containerization, no APIs, no cloud services, no observability. Every technology in the stack is end-of-life or unsupported. The application requires fundamental re-architecture across all modernization pathways before it can operate in a cloud-native environment.

findings.description: Application is a monolithic Win32 desktop executable with no service decomposition — cannot be deployed as a cloud-native service
No API layer exists — business logic is tightly coupled to the GUI form with direct database file access over SMB
No externalized configuration — database paths and credentials are hardcoded constants in source
No health checks, readiness probes, or graceful shutdown — incompatible with orchestrated environments
No stateless design — application holds a persistent ADO connection for the lifetime of the form
No 12-factor app principles followed — environment-specific values baked into the binary
Single-form architecture means minimal internal coupling to untangle during re-architecture

recommended_actions: Re-implement business logic as a web service (REST API on AWS Lambda or Amazon ECS) with externalized configuration
Adopt microservices or modular monolith architecture with defined API contracts
Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store or AWS Secrets Manager for configuration

findings.description: VB6 runtime requires Windows with compatibility shim — cannot run in a standard Linux container
No Dockerfile, no container image, no container registry configuration
Application depends on SMB file share (mapped drive S:\) for database access — not portable to container networking
No build automation — application compiled manually on a single developer's machine using the VB6 IDE
Crystal Reports 8.5 runtime dependency requires GUI-mode Windows installation — incompatible with headless containers
Small codebase (single form file) would simplify a ground-up rewrite targeting a containerizable runtime

recommended_actions: Rewrite in a containerizable language/framework (Python/FastAPI, Java/Spring Boot, .NET 8)
Build container images with Amazon ECR and deploy via Amazon ECS or Amazon EKS
Replace Crystal Reports with Amazon QuickSight

findings.description: Visual Basic 6.0 is proprietary, unsupported (EOL 2008), with no open-source runtime or compiler
Microsoft Access 2003 (.mdb) is a proprietary closed-format database with no open-source equivalent driver support
Crystal Reports 8.5 is proprietary reporting software with no migration path to open source in place
Microsoft Jet OLEDB 4.0 data provider is Windows-only and proprietary — no cross-platform alternative
No open-source tooling in the stack — no OSS build tools, test frameworks, or libraries

recommended_actions: Migrate from VB6 to an open-source language and framework (Python, Node.js, Java, or .NET on Linux)
Replace Microsoft Access with PostgreSQL (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL or Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)
Replace Crystal Reports with open-source alternatives (Apache Superset, Metabase) or Amazon QuickSight

findings.description: Primary database is Microsoft Access 2003 (.mdb) on SMB file share — file-based database with no server process, no ACID guarantees under concurrency, and monthly corruption events
Reporting database is SQL Server 2012, past end-of-extended-support — no longer receiving security patches
Database credentials hardcoded in source — incompatible with managed database IAM authentication
No connection pooling — each application instance opens a direct persistent connection
Raw SQL with string concatenation (SQL injection vulnerability) — no parameterized queries or ORM
Nightly DTS/SSIS sync between Access and SQL Server is fragile and undocumented
Simple data model (single Customers table visible) should make schema migration straightforward

recommended_actions: Migrate from Access .mdb to Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL or MySQL) or Amazon Aurora
Migrate SQL Server 2012 to Amazon RDS for SQL Server (current version) or Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
Implement AWS IAM database authentication and store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager
Replace DTS/SSIS sync with AWS DMS or event-driven data replication

findings.description: Reporting relies on Crystal Reports 8.5 — unsupported software that cannot be installed on new machines
Analytics data pipeline is a nightly DTS/SSIS package syncing Access to SQL Server 2012 — no streaming, no real-time analytics
No data warehouse or data lake architecture — reporting runs directly against an operational database copy
No BI tooling beyond Crystal Reports — no dashboards, no self-service analytics
Simple data model means migration to a modern analytics platform would be straightforward

recommended_actions: Replace Crystal Reports with Amazon QuickSight for interactive dashboards and reporting
Implement data pipelines using AWS Glue or Amazon Kinesis to feed Amazon Redshift or Amazon Athena
Establish a data lake on Amazon S3 for historical analysis and ML-ready datasets

findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline — application is compiled manually on a single developer's machine
No automated testing — zero test files, zero test frameworks, zero test coverage
Deployment is manual EXE copy to each laptop — no installer, no package management, no automated distribution
No infrastructure-as-code — all infrastructure (file server, SQL Server) is manually provisioned
No version control workflow — single developer model with no branching strategy or code review process
No environment separation — no dev/staging/prod environments; single shared .mdb is production
.gitignore present indicates some git usage, but no CI integration

recommended_actions: Implement CI/CD with AWS CodePipeline, AWS CodeBuild, and AWS CodeDeploy
Adopt infrastructure-as-code with AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK
Implement automated testing at unit, integration, and end-to-end levels
Establish environment separation (dev/staging/prod) with AWS accounts or VPC isolation

findings.description: No API layer for AI/ML services to integrate with — no programmatic interface for inference or data exchange
No structured data pipeline — data trapped in Access .mdb file format on a network share, inaccessible to ML platforms
No event-driven architecture — cannot trigger AI workflows based on data changes or user actions
No feature store or ML model serving infrastructure
Data quality unknown — no validation, no schema enforcement, potential duplicates from lack of idempotency
CRM domain (customer records) is well-suited for AI enrichment (lead scoring, churn prediction) once data is accessible

recommended_actions: After establishing an API layer and managed database, integrate Amazon Bedrock for generative AI capabilities
Use Amazon SageMaker for predictive models (lead scoring, churn prediction) on CRM data
Implement Amazon Personalize for customer engagement recommendations
Build data pipelines to Amazon S3 to enable ML training on historical customer data
